query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Infiltrating the surface pores of ZrB2 components with 10 vol % elemental silicon to form a dense ZrB2–Si layer will create a continuous Si-rich barrier at the molten‐aluminum interface, reducing the corrosion rate by at least 50 % relative to untreated ZrB2 when exposed to molten Al–12 wt % Si at 700 °C for 100 h under inert atmosphere.
generation.material_initial_state: Hot-pressed ZrB2 components (≈90 % theoretical density) with open surface porosity
generation.intervention: Pressure infiltration of 10 vol % elemental Si into surface pores (1450 °C, 1 h, 5 MPa argon) to form a Si-enriched surface layer
generation.conditions: Immersion in molten Al–12 wt % Si alloy at 700 °C for 100 h under flowing argon, no mechanical load
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous, ~10 µm thick Si-rich surface barrier layer
generation.mechanism: The Si barrier lowers wettability and slows dissolution of underlying ZrB2 by molten aluminum, limiting direct contact and intermetallic formation
generation.predicted_outcome: ≈50 % reduction in mass loss compared to untreated ZrB2 after 100 h
generation.baseline: Untreated ZrB2 exposed under identical molten-Al conditions
generation.boundary: Effective between 650–750 °C and exposure times up to 200 h in inert atmosphere; above 800 °C the Si barrier may degrade
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; mechanism inferred from analogous Si-infiltrated boride composites but not yet directly tested on ZrB2 vs molten Al

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of ZrB2 coupons (untreated and Si-infiltrated). Expose both to molten Al–12 wt % Si at 700 °C for 100 h under argon. Measure mass loss and examine cross-sectional microstructure by SEM/EDS to assess barrier integrity.
measurements: Barrier thickness and continuity by SEM/EDS
Extent of Al penetration at interface
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Si-infiltrated samples show less than 25 % reduction in mass loss vs untreated baseline, or fail to form a continuous Si-rich layer, the hypothesis is falsified.
